notes: Field-by-field verdict on the 15 fields the create sibling flagged, using TR-9062 (subject, fresh) cross-checked against TR-9061 (linked to TP-1616) and TR-9058 (older, readonly): ALL 15 are also absent here — id, uuid, type, owner, environment, overall_progress_by_status_id, test_cases_count, is_automation, observability_url, metadata, assignee_imported, is_dynamic (top-level), test_plans, self_ui_link, links.detail. This is a clean match with the create sibling's gap list, confirming the pattern flagged in the task: this looks like a contract-wide over-declaration for the test_run entity rather than a create-specific projection gap, since the read path (which has every reason to return a fuller record than a create response) still omits the exact same 15 fields. Two of those need a caveat rather than a flat ABSENT: (1) is_dynamic does not exist at top level, but a field of the same name exists nested at filter_test_cases.is_dynamic (boolean) — so the name is real, just relocated and never at the path the schema declares it; (2) test_plans (plural array) never appears in any read, but when a run actually carries a plan link (TR-9061), a related-but-different field test_plan (singular object) shows up instead, with id as a STRING ("TP-1616") rather than the declared integer — this is exactly the test_plan-entity-wide drift pattern batch 4 already caught on the five dedicated test_plan capabilities, now showing up a sixth time inside get_test_run_v2's own nested shape. overall_progress is the one exception to 'identical to create': it IS present on read (unlike create, where it was fully missing), but its actual shape ({"Untested": 4}, one capitalized sparse key) is incompatible with the declared shape (seven fixed lowercase keys always present) — so even where the read path fills in a create gap, it fills it in with the wrong contract. assignee: returned as a plain string (email) or null, never the declared object with id/browserstack_user_id/full_name/group_id/onboarded — identical to the create finding; DRIFT, not a create-only quirk. Numeric/uuid run id: NONE appears anywhere in any of the three reads, at the run level or nested. TR-NNNN (via `identifier`) is the only run identifier on the whole v2 surface for this capability. The contract is not merely silent about this — its own guidance text explicitly says 'The run's id field comes back as the TR-NNN string; the integer lives in uuid. Take uuid whenever you need a numeric run id downstream,' which is actively wrong: neither id nor uuid is ever present, so following that guidance fails. filter_test_cases, urls, and links.test_cases: all three are returned and are genuinely UNDECLARED in this capability's own contract (schema only declares links.{self,detail}, nothing else) — matches the create finding exactly, same undeclared trio. filter_test_cases.is_dynamic type: boolean (false) on TR-9062, TR-9061, and TR-9058 alike — a third/fourth data point agreeing with list_test_runs_v2 and update_test_run_v2 (boolean), reinforcing get_test_plan_test_runs_v2 (integer) as the outlier. Additional undeclared surface beyond the create-comparison checklist: the response also returns a full `test_cases` array (rich nested objects: case_type, latest_result_id, execution_id, folder_path, urls.self, etc.) and an `issues` array — neither mentioned anywhere in the contract, flat returns or nested schema; issues was empty in all three runs, so its item shape is UNVERIFIED, not cleared. Error envelope: a `minify=true` query param reproducibly triggers a 500 with a literal null body (no {success,error} envelope at all) on two consecutive attempts against TR-9062 — status 500 is in the declared set, but the body shape is not, adding an eighth confirmed error-envelope mismatch to the systemic tally; this is a genuine 500, distinct from the preprod status-0 flake, and is a real functional bug in the minify path specifically (default/no-minify requests succeeded every time, 3/3 runs). No writes were made to TR-9062 or the sibling fixtures; only reads were performed.
